title: Universal cycle constructions for k-subsets and k-multisets
summary: A universal cycle for a set S of combinatorial objects is a cyclic sequence of length |S|that contains a representation of each element in S exactly once as a substring. If S is the set of k-subsets of [n] = {1, 2, . . . , n}, it is well-known that universal cycles do not always exists when applying a simple string representation, where 12 or 21 could represent the subset {1, 2}. Similarly, if S is the set of k-multisets of [n], it is also known that universal cycles do not always exist using a similar representation, where 112, 121, or 211 could represent the multiset {1, 1, 2}.
